messages:
Lina: Hi team, quick Q 1 1 I got married in Spain last week. Open enrollment ended. Can I add my spouse midyear even though they don't have a US SSN yet?
Sam (People Ops): Congrats Lina! :confetti_ball: Yes, marriage is a Qualifying Life Event. You have 30 days from the marriage date to request a midyear enrollment. Foreign spouses without a US SSN are commonwe can still enroll them.
Lina: Awesome. What docs do you need? The certificate is in Spanish. Also curious about effective date and if premiums will be backdated.
Sam (People Ops): We'll need: 1) certified marriage certificate (scan), 2) English translation + notarization if certificate isn't in English, 3) government ID for spouse, 4) proof of shared residence (if available) or a signed affidavit, 5) foreign tax ID (e.g., NIF) or "No SSN" affidavit.
Nora: If the spouse later gets a US SSN, we ask you to provide it so payroll/benefits can update tax reporting. For now the foreign tax ID is fine for enrollment.
Lina: Cool. How about effective date and payroll impacts? Will premiums be deducted retroactively?
Sam (People Ops): Effective date is usually the marriage date (the QLE date) once docs are approved. Premiums will be prorated back to the effective date; payroll will adjust next pay cycle after benefits update. If you elect HSA contributions, you must update pretax elections by the payroll cutoff to affect the next paycheck.
Payroll Bot: FYI payroll cutoff for changes is 8am PT on the Thursday before pay run. Changes submitted after approval may reflect on the following cycle.
Lina: Any restrictions on FSA? I have a Dependent Care FSA and a Health Care FSA.
Sam (People Ops): Health Care FSA can be updated for a QLE; Dependent Care FSA can only change if you add an eligible dependent and you claim the spouse as a dependent for tax purposes. We'll confirm eligibility case-by-case.
Lina: What about dental/vision and life insurance?
Benefits Admin: Dental and vision can be added through the same QLE process. Dependent life/AD&D requires beneficiary forms for the spouse; we'll email the form when we create your case.
Lina: Where do I upload docs? I don't want to email attachments with personal info.
Sam (People Ops): Use the Benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/portal -> "Report a Life Event" -> attach documents. If you'd rather, DM me and I can create the case and give you a secure upload link.
Lina: Great, thanks. Anything else I should know because spouse is abroad for now?
Sam (People Ops): Two small notes: 1) If your spouse has other local coverage and you're trying to switch based on loss of other coverage, we'll need proof of the loss. 2) For international addresses we sometimes flag for manual review; allow 5 business days for verification.
Nora: Also for tax forms: W-2 reporting uses SSN when provided. Until an SSN is added, payroll may need extra paperwork for tax withholding, but we won't delay coverage.
Lina: Submitted the portal case and uploaded scanned certificate + translation just now. Case ID: 2026-PL-337.
Sam (People Ops): Got it, Lina. I'll fast-track the review and DM you if anything else is missing. Expect the enrollment link within 24 hours and 14 days to finalize elections.
Lina: Thank you!! :sparkles:
Benefits Admin: Reminder: if you want spouse added to HSA-eligible plan, confirm HSA contribution election once you get the enrollment link; otherwise pre-tax contributions won't change automatically.
Lina: Noted. I'll wait for the link and choose same plans. Thanks everyone.
